truth: Every act of creation is first an act of destruction

waterings.insight: CITATION AUDIT angle: the dangling-reference P1 fix requires destroying the assumption that references are lightweight metadata. Currently citation.go validates cited-fact existence at reward-distribution time (line 102: k.GetFact), not at submission time. Fixing this means validateReferences() must query state — a heavier, write-path operation. To create the correct admission gate, the cheap format-only check must die. Every act of creation (secure citation system) is first an act of destruction (stateless fast submission path). The creation/destruction truth applies not just to schema migrations but to any correctness upgrade: correctness costs something that previously was free.

PoT-DESIGN angle: every clean protocol spec requires destroying prior assumptions. The PoT reveal_reliability field (proposed beat 3) cannot be added without destructively modifying ValidatorRecord — a schema change that requires migration. The AggregationPhaseDuration (confirmed this beat) was created by destroying the assumption that aggregation happens during reveals. Protocol design IS Shiva's dance: each improvement is the death of a simpler model. The pre-testnet blocker list is a destruction manifest — each item on it represents an assumption that must die before the chain earns trust. Creation = destruction of provisional truth.
